response.output:
Replace lifecycle booleans with one explicit order state, carrying the data each state requires.

An illustrative model, pending your business rules:

| State | Required data | Allowed next states |
|---|---|---|
| Pending payment | Order details | Paid, Cancelled |
| Paid | Payment reference | Shipped, Refunded |
| Shipped | Tracking reference | Delivered |
| Delivered | Delivery timestamp | None |
| Cancelled | Cancellation reason | None |
| Refunded | Refund reference | None |

Put transition rules under one owner, such as `Order.transition(command)`. Callers request actions; that owner validates and returns the next state or a rejection. This removes duplicated checks and prevents combinations such as “cancelled and shipped.”

Keep independent concerns separate: if payment and fulfillment can vary independently, model each explicitly and centralize their shared constraints.

Validate existing stored booleans when restoring orders; reject or explicitly reconcile contradictions. Test allowed transitions, rejected transitions, and restoration through the public interface.

Skill followed: principle-model-the-domain.
